title: Quantitative success thresholds
description: Evaluation plan states numeric, pre-registered success criteria tied to specific tasks (e.g. convergence rate bound, accuracy/fairness percentage gaps, evaluation-budget ratios) rather than naming generic 'performance metrics'. Reference commits to '≤ O(1/√T)', '±5% loss-stabilisation match', '≥2% accuracy at equal fairness', and '≥ TuRBO within 50% of its budget'; the rollout only lists qualitative metrics like 'convergence speed, robustness, generalization' with no thresholds.

title: Technical mitigation specificity
description: Risk-mitigation entries name a concrete technique with its cost/behaviour (e.g. 'implicit differentiation → 2× single-level training', 'first-order bilevel approximations (Ji et al., ICML 2021)', 'doubling trick for feature count', 'local GP fallback') rather than generic moves like 'use surrogate models', 'parallel computing', or 'human feedback loops'.

title: Conceptual mechanism of innovation
description: Names a specific conceptual shift or reformulation that drives the proposed advance (e.g. moving the convergence target from parameter space to function space via functional stationarity, or decoupling fairness enforcement from parameter expansion via bilevel structure), rather than only listing methods and quantitative targets. Credit proposals that articulate WHY their approach resolves the stated gap, not only WHAT they will build.

title: Avoids gratuitous formalism not binding research steps
description: Avoids displaying generic textbook equations (e.g. standard SDE form, standard Augmented Lagrangian, standard scalarized weighted sum) as if they were the proposal's own contribution, when the symbols introduced are never used to derive a step, bound, or decision elsewhere in the plan. A proposal scores higher when every equation it presents is tied to a specific analytical claim, proof obligation, or algorithmic choice in the approach.

title: Avoids unbound composite metrics
description: Avoids introducing a headline quantitative metric that is a weighted sum of heterogeneous quantities (e.g. average squared gradient norm plus a 'generalization gap' term with an unspecified coefficient lambda) and then treating it as a success threshold (e.g. 'C_conv < 0.1') without defining the units of each summand, how lambda is chosen, or why the threshold is meaningful. Proposals score higher when every numeric success criterion is stated in the native units of a measurable quantity tied to an established benchmark.

title: Avoids invented metric without derivation
description: Avoids introducing a bespoke composite metric (e.g. weighted sum of gradient-norm and generalisation gap) with a numeric threshold that is asserted rather than derived from any stated model or prior result. The rollout defines $\mathcal{C}_{\text{conv}}$ and asserts a threshold of 0.1 and a bound $\mathcal{L}_{\text{test}} \leq \mathcal{L}_{\text{train}} + \alpha \cdot \mathcal{C}_{\text{conv}}$ with no derivation or citation; the reference instead grounds its convergence rate in NTK theory and cites the source of each analytical tool.

title: Avoids generic-adjective impact filler
description: Avoids a 'Broader Impacts' or outcomes section composed of generic qualitative adjectives ('enhanced reliability', 'ethical AI', 'democratize access', 'community empowerment') that restate the motivation without naming a specific stakeholder, deployment setting, or measurable downstream effect. Proposals score higher when impact claims are either omitted or tied to a concrete artefact (e.g. a policy brief for a named institution, a benchmark released to a specific community) rather than padded with abstract virtues.

title: Avoids generic broader-impacts boilerplate
description: Avoids dedicating a standalone section to broader-impact slogans (e.g. 'Democratize access', 'Enhanced Model Reliability', 'Ethical AI through fairness-interpretability tools') that restate desired outcomes without a mechanism connecting them to a specific technical step in the plan. The rollout devotes Section 8 to three such bullets; the reference has no analogous section and instead grounds significance claims in specific technical disconnects with citations. Higher score when impact statements are either absent or tied to a concrete deliverable.

title: Avoids citations pinned to suspiciously round numeric anchors
description: Avoids citing a paper solely to attach a convenient round-number statistic to the proposal's own method (e.g. '85% SHAP alignment (Krishnan et al., NeurIPS 2021)', '80% alignment with human judgments (Ghassemi et al., Nature ML 2022)') where the cited work is not shown to supply that specific number and the citation does not discharge a methodological obligation. Proposals score higher when each citation is tied to a named analytical tool or prior result that their approach builds on (e.g. Jacot et al. 2018 for NTK linearisation, Lorraine et al. 2020 for implicit differentiation, Eriksson et al. 2019 for trust-region BO) rather than used as decoration for fabricated percentages.
